text: おれの　ポケモン　どく　くらったまま　あるいてたら　ちから　つき　おったで！

structure.jp: どく　くらったまま
ちから　つき　おったで！
structure.en: it went and ran out of strength!

patterns.name: 〜まま
patterns.explanation: まま after a past verb means staying in that state without fixing it. どく　くらったまま = 'still poisoned, as it was'.

patterns.name: 〜たら
patterns.explanation: The past form with ら added means 'when' that happened; あるいてたら is the casual short form of あるいていたら. あるいてたら = 'when I was walking along'.

patterns.name: 〜おる
patterns.explanation: In Kansai dialect, おる added to a verb shows the speaker is annoyed at what someone did, and で at the end is the dialect's よ. ちから　つき　おったで = 'it went and fainted on me!'.
